Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC MAP: environment bootstrapping checklist & ownership

Tom — great to meet last week. As discussed, I sketched a short bootstrapping checklist for the POC environment so we can align responsibilities and close on the first milestone (org activation + API access). I attached a starter workbook (map-bootstrapping-v1.xlsx) — feel free to edit. High-level items below: 

- Org setup: create customer org in our console, invite SRE and app owners (we need one admin and one read-only observer)
- API keys: decide on ephemeral tokens vs. long-lived service account tokens; we recommend ephemeral for the trial
- IP allowlist: LimeHealth to provide CIDR ranges (we'll confirm which egress IPs from your side require whitelisting)
- VPC peering: two-stage — (1) test peering for staging (small CIDR), (2) production peering if we proceed

Questions for you: can you confirm who will own firewall changes and whether your network team prefers a shared peering subnet or dedicated peer? Also, do you want us to pre-provision a set of ephemeral API keys for initial tests?

Next steps I propose: 
1) You review the attached workbook and drop owners in the "Owner" column
2) Jordan and I schedule a 30-min technical handoff with your network/SRE (we can do Tue/Wed morning PST)
3) We run a short connectivity test within 48 hours of key provisioning

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

Hi Tom / Priya — quick technical notes to help your network/SRE prep before the handoff: 

API keys / tokens
- Recommended: ephemeral bearer tokens with 1h default TTL for user-driven tests, refresh via our auth endpoint. For longer-running CI jobs, use a short-lived service account token with a 12-hour rotation window.
- Minimal scopes: generate_token (issue ephemeral), read_models, generate_inference. If you'll use embeddings/reranking add embeddings:write.
- We'll provide a small CLI helper to rotate tokens for the POC (I'll attach the step-by-step in the peering doc).

IP allowlist
- For quick verification tests you can allow the following egress ranges from Redwood: 34.196.25.0/24, 34.196.26.0/24 (we can narrow during staging).
- Use network-allowlist-template.txt (attached) to drop into your firewall rule set.

VPC peering
- Two phases: peer a /27 for staging (low blast radius) and if accepted, expand to /24 for production.
- Requirements: route propagation must be enabled on your side; confirm whether your cloud account requires route table updates or if you use transit gateway.
- See vpc-peering-ops.pdf (attached) for a checklist: request, acceptance, route updates, security group checks, NAT gateway considerations.

Attachments: vpc-peering-ops.pdf (diagram + ops checklist), network-allowlist-template.txt

I'll be on the tech call to walk through the peering checklist — propose Wed 16 Jun 09:00 PST. If that works for Priya, send calendar invite and include any internal ticket ID you want us to reference.

Cheers,
Jordan
